key_insight: TIDER improves long-horizon memory retrieval by first localizing the relevant time window, then using that temporal anchor to recover evidence that semantic search alone would miss.
engineering_relevance: For agent systems with growing long-term memory, adding an explicit temporal retrieval stage can reduce false matches from semantically similar but time-misaligned events.
method: RL-trained temporal interval locator predicts where evidence occurs in time
Temporal windows form a dedicated retrieval channel that narrows candidate search
Temporal and semantic candidates are merged and reranked by proximity to the predicted window
evidence_signal: On long-horizon memory benchmarks, TIDER reaches 61.52% on LifeBench and 78.96% on LoCoMo, outperforming prior methods by +8.82% and +3.66%, respectively.
watch_item: The approach depends on a learned window locator, so performance may be sensitive to noisy reward design, retrieval granularity, or memory timelines that are poorly structured.
paper_title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
